study.question: Does synchronous category/brand match-transition dependence within each action add useful information beyond the incumbent separate field/action summaries? Observation: r0038-basis_observed_raw exactly reproduced incumbent AUC .6209487954658293; observed_residual .6206196324377012 and both constant bases .6206033050204942 failed to improve it. Source audit: incumbent per-field transition helpers never form a four-state joint field-transition table. Earlier r0002 joint same-event counts (.6183522161) did not beat factorized counts (.6183741960); that negative result makes another generic joint-count claim unwarranted. This proposal instead tests cross-time transition coupling against controls preserving both per-field transition marginals.
study.hypothesis: On the fixed causal prefix, dependence between category-match changes and brand-match changes within the same action can provide incremental target relevance beyond separate field trajectories. A four-state joint transition readout should outperform a product of its two binary field-transition marginals, especially for chronological rather than permutation-expected transitions. This is a provisional representational hypothesis, not a causal interpretation or a claim that joint matching is always useful.

nearest_work.difference: Retain existing category/brand-adapted target attention unchanged. DIN primary relaxes normalization whereas this inherited implementation uses softmax. New readout is an explicit action-conditioned four-state field-transition distribution and product-marginal replacement; no exact DIN reproduction or novelty priority claim.

README verifies histories lack item IDs. Use only supplied category/brand equality, action and causal ages; no item journey, matching supervision or DMR-paper mechanism reproduction. Publisher full text unavailable; priority remains unverified.

Early joint-count branch is a negative local antecedent; current source models switches separately per field/action and action transitions separately per field. New 4x4 role transitions couple both fields at both ends, and control preserves their complete 2x2 transition marginals on exactly the same action/timestamp population.

inherited_components: Exact complete incumbent candidate.py source, including field embeddings, shared attention and static context queries
Original Adam, binary cross entropy, fixed data coverage and source initialization draws
Timestamp grouping principle: tie distributions rather than invented within-timestamp ordering
study.proposed_difference: Append64 deterministic features, 16 ordered old-role/new-role probabilities for each of pv/cart/fav/buy, scaled .5 and read by64 zero-initialized columns of the existing first classifier layer. Role=2*category_match+brand_match; only events with both positive field IDs and both positive target IDs qualify. Group equal raw ages within each action, average four-role one-hots in ties, sort newest first. J=sum(p_old outer p_new)/(G-1), gated G>1. E=(S outer S-Q)/(G*(G-1)) is exact expected adjacency under uniform permutation of distinct timestamp groups. For each J/E, reshape indices as(c_old,b_old,c_new,b_new), marginalize to Mc and Mb, and replace by F=M_c tensor M_b. Joint/order factors yield four matched variants. The product is a descriptive independent-transition distribution, not an executable surrogate event sequence. All four matrices computed in every variant; no parameters, RNG draws, loss or optimizer beyond identical64 classifier columns.
predictions: Primary: AUC(joint_ordered)>AUC(factorized_ordered) and AUC(joint_ordered)>AUC(incumbent); joint_ordered>joint_exchangeable would additionally support usefulness of order in the new readout.

Stronger timing-specific evidence requires positive interaction [AUC(JO)-AUC(FO)]-[AUC(JE)-AUC(FE)], then paired-seed repetition. A main effect shared by JO and JE supports composition/coupling only, not temporal synchronization.

All matrices have total mass1 on common G>1 support and0 elsewhere. Product controls preserve both complete binary field-transition marginals within float32 tolerance; permutation means are symmetric. Candidate-supplied first512 diagnostics should show nonzero joint-product distance and sufficient supported/nonconstant roles before a null is interpreted as a useful mechanism test.

Exploratory frozen host slices: differences may concentrate in long histories and action-present slices. Report sample/positive/negative counts already supplied; do not treat small/missing-field strata or first512 diagnostics as performance evidence.
falsifiers: If JO does not beat FO or incumbent on primary AUC, this implementation does not support incremental joint-transition benefit; improved Logloss alone does not satisfy primary prediction.
If chronological advantage and interaction are absent, do not claim temporal binding even if unordered joint features help.
Near-zero coupling distance, rare positive match roles or inadequate per-action support makes the discrimination weak rather than a refutation of all coupling mechanisms.

Any parent feature drift, unequal support/capacity/initialization, nonfinite logits, information-boundary violation, marginal identity failure above numerical tolerance or cap overrun invalidates attribution and requires preserving the failed receipt.
alternative_explanations: Extra classifier parameters or feature scale/conditioning could explain improvement; four cells match capacity, scale, calculations, optimizer and initialization, but incumbent comparison alone cannot isolate them.
Joint tables encode contemporaneous role composition and endpoint frequencies as well as transition dependence; unordered joint control helps distinguish these.
Factorization is nonlinear, so F(E[J]) differs from E[F(J)]; factorial effects are descriptive controlled contrasts, not a causal decomposition.
Category-brand taxonomy dependence and repeated advertising exposure can create correlations without intent progression. No item IDs or causal user-state claim.
Pair-valid population differs from each inherited per-field population; every new cell uses the same population, but attribution against the incumbent includes this addition.
Sparse buy/cart/fav support, supplied128-event truncation, shared-field IDs, seed variation and repeated validation selection may explain nulls or small gains.
